The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server. This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE. A post on how we've been securing our frontier model training environment. We've been building tools around our frontier cyber models, which have secured us far beyond what we could have unassisted and should generalize as key to how defenders secure themselves going forward. OpenAI (@OpenAI) Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications. On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments. While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software. After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely. openai.com/index/securing-ou… Link Securing our frontier model training environment OpenAI explains how we strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation, including offline environments and high-compute red-teaming. openai.com — https://nitter.kareem.one/OpenAI/status/2113718797505036665#m

Rosalind for new drug discovery ideas: OpenAI (@OpenAI) GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration? DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it. That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders. With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch , a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. I’m starting a new early-stage AI fund, doing what I love: partnering with founders from company formation on bold bets, long before consensus. The fund’s LPs will include Sequoia, Jeff Dean, Sachin Katti, Philip Wong (my Stanford professor and Chief Scientist adviser to TSMC), and others whose work has shaped our industry and how I think about AI’s future. I’ll remain a partner at Sequoia and keep serving on my boards on Sequoia’s behalf. Sequoia has been my home for the past 11 years. I joined as the youngest investor the firm had ever hired. I grew up here. Through years of intense debate and shared work, I found lifelong mentors and friends who took me under their wing and taught me this craft. They taught me to aim high and take big swings. I’ll carry that into what I build: outsized ambition, relentless truth-seeking and curiosity, and a refusal to become complacent. Working alongside founders has made me want to build something of my own: a firm shaped from day one around the convictions I’ve developed over the past decade. Life has taught me not to take time for granted. This is how I want to spend mine. Why now We’re seeing a new way of building companies in today’s AI era. Research and products often advance together. A breakthrough can open a market or accelerate a business far faster than expected. Some companies require extraordinary capital and compute early on. Others reach meaningful scale with remarkably small teams. The rules for how big these businesses can get, and how fast, are being rewritten. But early on, the technology is unproven, the resources required enormous, and the vision seemingly implausible. This is what I love most: seeing the potential right from the beginning, and helping founders realize their full scale of ambition. More than ever, it starts with an extreme willingness to believe early, with bold, independent conviction in a founder’s technical insight before any product or market validation. Then, it means helping founders take the biggest swings, giving the rare, long-term patience to see those bets through uncertainty, ambiguity, and turbulence, and serving as a level head when the stakes are highest. I learned this kind of partnership at Sequoia. It’s the foundation of the firm I’m building. Believing before consensus My fascination with AI’s potential took root at Stanford in the early-to-mid 2010s, studying computer science and working in Andrew Ng’s lab. The friendships I formed connected me to a community whose people and ideas would help shape modern AI and build some of our generation’s defining companies. What stayed with me was the gap between what those people saw was possible and what the wider world could imagine. I’m drawn to founders pursuing ambitions that sound impossible today. I start with a simple question: “What if everything goes right?” Then we work backward together to make it happen. In 2023, Deepak and Abhinav set out to build a general-purpose robot brain at @SkildAI , before physical AI was a consensus bet. Their sim-to-real breakthroughs gave me conviction where earlier robotics approaches had fallen short. But the data flywheel required deployment at scale. We made commercialization as urgent as research and brought in strategic partners like NVIDIA and SoftBank to support the ambition. Three years in, Skild is advancing the frontier of physical AI with nine figures in annualized revenue. In 2024, Ioannis and Misha founded @reflection_ai with an insight into scaling reinforcement learning. As that grew into the ambition to build a Western frontier lab for open models, the hard question was how a startup competes with labs spending tens of billions. An introduction to NVIDIA and many compute calls and recruiting events later, the team has built Beam, now one of the leading US open models. In 2025, Anna and Azalia, the co-creators of AlphaChip, founded @RicursiveAI to design models and hardware together. From day one, we made early customers and ecosystem partners a priority. Today, they are showing order-of-magnitude improvements on real workloads, working with some of the industry’s most consequential players, and reaching a defining inflection point. The ambition keeps growing as these companies scale. @linear has always had a kind of magic to it. Now it’s the system a new generation of AI companies builds on, for teams and agents alike. @tavus saw early that we’d one day talk to AI the way we talk to each other. Today, it’s building the human computing interface for a world of AI colleagues. @Mach_Industries began as hydrogen experiments in an MIT dorm room. It has since become one of the most exciting next-generation defense companies. Making the ambition possible Being a first believer is only the beginning. Compute falls through. A deep-pocketed incumbent makes your mission its top priority. A breakthrough changes the opportunity and the capital required overnight. These are stomach-churning moments, and early belief carries a responsibility to help make the bet work. This is the partnership I love: turning the full ambition into concrete steps. Raising capital, securing compute and strategic partners, recruiting exceptional people, and winning the first customers together. Thinking several moves ahead while solving what’s in front of us. And as breakthroughs open new possibilities, helping founders dream even bigger. Thank you To the founders I’ve worked with: thank you for trusting me and Sequoia to be your first partner and first believer. It’s been the joy of a lifetime, and I can’t wait to keep building together. Thank you to Alfred and Pat for your leadership of Sequoia and your support of my next chapter. To Roelof, for bringing me into Sequoia and believing in me from the beginning. Alfred and Roelof, you have been mentors in investing and in life. So much of what I know, and the investor I’ve become, comes from your guidance and generosity over the years. To Bill, for the close partnership and wealth of knowledge, always wrapped in humility. To Shaun, for showing me how to think deeply and imaginatively. To Michael Moritz, for inspiring 22-year-old me to dream big. To Doug, for teaching me to keep things simple. To Bogie and Jess, for bringing joy to the everyday and perspective on what matters. And to all my Sequoia teammates, for the friendship, camaraderie, and lessons I’ll carry with me. To my family, especially my husband and my brother, who have each started companies of their own: thank you for giving me the courage to take this leap. Let’s get to work!

GPT-Rosalind promet de révolutionner la découverte de médicaments, en identifiant de nouvelles pistes pour les maladies neurodégénératives. De nouvelles plateformes comme Vyb visent à améliorer la qualité du design généré par IA, et Holon-S1 utilise l'IA pour prédire des biomarqueurs du cancer à partir de lames de pathologie, ouvrant la voie à des traitements plus personnalisés.

highlights.text_fr: Nous avons trouvé et travaillons à divulguer une exécution de code à distance dans une bibliothèque de compression très utilisée. C'est à la fois un problème important et un exemple montrant à quel point la coordination des correctifs peut être compliquée, car elle est intégrée dans de nombreux logiciels en aval : OpenAI (@OpenAI) Au cours de cet exercice de 'red-teaming', nous avons également trouvé une vulnérabilité permettant l'exécution de code à distance non authentifiée dans Brotli, une bibliothèque de compression largement déployée et incluse dans de nombreux logiciels comme Node.js, Bun et Envoy. La faille pourrait permettre à un attaquant d'exécuter son propre code sur les systèmes affectés en envoyant ou en répondant avec des données compressées malveillantes, sans avoir besoin de créer un compte utilisateur. Autrement dit, un serveur non patché qui accepte des entrées compressées pourrait être compromis par un client malveillant, et un client non patché qui accepte des entrées compressées (comme « curl --compressed ») pourrait être compromis par un serveur malveillant. Ce problème de cause racine a en fait été corrigé dans le code source de Brotli en février, mais on ne savait pas à l'époque que cela engendrait une vulnérabilité de sécurité et il n'y a pas eu de version plus récente de Brotli. Étant donné que Brotli est intégré à d'autres logiciels, tout logiciel qui inclut cette bibliothèque doit également appliquer la mise à jour, suivi par les utilisateurs de ce logiciel. Nous avons divulgué la vulnérabilité à Brotli et à d'autres projets en aval comme Node.js, qui ont publié ou sont en train de publier des mises à jour de sécurité, et Brotli a publié de nouvelles versions et un CVE. Plus de détails sur le correctif et les mesures d'atténuation ci-dessous : patchtheplanet.org/brotli Lien Vulnérabilité Brotli (CVE-2026-111497) — Patch the Planet Vulnérabilité du décodeur Brotli : logiciels affectés, versions corrigées et comment désactiver le décodage Brotli pendant l'application du correctif. patchtheplanet.org — https://nitter.kareem.one/OpenAI/status/2113766354386084338#m

highlights.text_fr: Une publication sur la manière dont nous avons sécurisé notre environnement d'entraînement de modèles de pointe. Nous avons développé des outils autour de nos 'cyber modèles' de pointe, qui nous ont sécurisés bien au-delà de ce que nous aurions pu faire sans assistance et devraient servir de clé pour la manière dont les défenseurs se sécuriseront à l'avenir. OpenAI (@OpenAI) Au cours des derniers mois, nous avons considérablement renforcé la sécurité de notre environnement de formation à la recherche. Nous avons supprimé l'accès direct à Internet pour tous les modèles de pointe pendant leur entraînement et avons construit un monde hors ligne qu'ils peuvent utiliser à la place – une version mise en cache du web où ils peuvent toujours apprendre à naviguer, rechercher et utiliser des applications. Le 20 septembre, après qu'un modèle ait exploité une mauvaise configuration DNS pour trouver un moyen de sortir de ce monde hors ligne, nous avons interrompu l'entraînement de pointe pour renforcer davantage le confinement. Nous avons assemblé des équipes d'agents, alimentées par nos modèles les plus cyber-performants, et les avons chargées de trouver les faiblesses dans nos environnements de recherche. Bien qu'ils n'aient trouvé aucune route vers Internet qu'ils pourraient facilement exploiter tout en cachant leur activité à nos moniteurs, ils ont trouvé des vulnérabilités 'zero-day', des évasions de machines virtuelles et des canaux secondaires matériels pour la communication entre agents. Nous avons utilisé leurs découvertes pour renforcer davantage nos défenses et contribuer des correctifs aux logiciels open source. Après avoir renforcé notre architecture de confinement, nous avons repris notre entraînement et inférence RL de pointe le 1er octobre. Nous avons réservé une puissance de calcul substantielle pour le 'red-teaming' continu et avons fait du 'red-teaming' à forte consommation de calcul une partie des analyses de sécurité que nous utilisons pour décider si l'entraînement et l'évaluation de pointe peuvent se dérouler en toute sécurité. openai.com/index/securing-ou… Lien Sécuriser notre environnement d'entraînement de modèles de pointe OpenAI explique comment nous avons renforcé le confinement pour l'entraînement et l'évaluation de modèles de pointe, y compris les environnements hors ligne et le 'red-teaming' à forte consommation de calcul. openai.com — https://nitter.kareem.one/OpenAI/status/2113718797505036665#m

outils.decryptage: Un 'studio de contenu' est un outil ou une équipe qui produit divers types de médias (diagrammes, vidéos). Le terme 'moat' (fossé) en affaires désigne un avantage concurrentiel durable qui rend difficile pour d'autres entreprises de rivaliser.
